conviction_note: Netting a mild negative tilt (a cyber-clean Q4 EBITDA run-rate that is roughly flat y/y and therefore makes the initial FY27 guide the whole print, a 13% SNAP enrollment collapse published after management last guided, and negative traffic at the two listed natural-channel retailers inside UNFI's Q4 window) against a stable largest customer, a company that raised its FY26 adjusted EPS guide midpoint from $1.90 to $2.50 over three quarters, and a three-week pull-forward of the report date; almost all of my negatives point the same way as the +6.97 put skew and the -6.65% run-in, so I hold the number to a fifth of the 12.5% implied and inside the 5.09% deadband rather than pretending to beat the option market.

findings.finding: UNFI's own narrowed FY26 guide implies Q4 adjusted EBITDA of $156-176mm, but the company itself quantified the prior-year Q4 as depressed by $40-50mm of cyber-incident adjusted EBITDA, so on a cyber-clean basis Q4 FY26 EBITDA is roughly flat to +13% (mid ~+3%) against reported growth of +34% to +52%, and against +23.4% in Q2 and +16.6% in Q3 — the underlying run-rate that has to support a ~$745-760mm FY27 guide on the way to the $800mm FY28 Investor Day target has decelerated to near zero.
findings.why_not_priced: The arithmetic requires stitching three documents together: 39-week actuals (26-week adj EBITDA $346mm from the 2026-03-10 8-K plus $183mm Q3 from the 2026-06-09 8-K = $529mm), the narrowed FY26 guide of $685-705mm, and the July 2025 8-K's $40-50mm cyber EBITDA quantification. If the market had done it, the published Q4 consensus would not be sitting exactly on the guide midpoint (rev $7.705bn vs guide-implied $7.590-7.790bn; EPS $0.612 vs guide-implied $0.45-0.65, i.e. the 81st percentile of the company's own range) — consensus is modelling the reported optic, not the clean run-rate, and there is no visible FY27 whisper on a name the aggregators show with 2 estimates.
findings.independence: Same-document cluster warning: the 39-week actuals and the guide come from UNFI's Q2/Q3 8-Ks, and the cyber quantification from the July 2025 8-K, so this is one arithmetic chain, not three findings. It shares its conclusion (FY27 guide risk) with the new-CFO finding below and the two should be read as overlapping. Independent corroboration of the FY28 anchor it is measured against: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1020859/000102085925000070/a2025investordaypressrelea.htm (Investor Day, 2025-12-10, ~$33bn sales / ~$800mm adjusted EBITDA / ~$300mm FCF by FY28).

findings.finding: SNAP enrollment fell from 42.2 million in May 2025 to 36.6 million in May 2026 (-13%, faster than CBO projected, with Arizona -55%, Florida -22%), and this data was published on 2026-08-21 — after UNFI last guided on 2026-06-09; UNFI's Conventional ($3.136bn) plus Retail ($515mm) segments were ~47% of Q3 FY26 net sales and are precisely the SNAP-exposed channels.
findings.why_not_priced: UNFI is modelled as a natural/organic growth story, not a SNAP name — its Q3 narrative and the sell-side framing are Natural segment growth and network optimisation, and management has never quantified SNAP exposure on a call. If this were priced into UNFI specifically you would see Conventional-segment estimates cut and the FY27 sales bridge debated; instead UNFI reiterated its FY26 midpoints on 2026-06-09 and the coverage that followed argued about the revenue miss, not the channel. The SNAP theme is priced into Kroger/Dollar General; it is not priced into the wholesaler two steps upstream.
findings.independence: Circana estimates total SNAP EBT will fall ~$10bn in 2026 versus 2025, a separate commercial estimate from a separate publisher: https://www.foodmanufacturing.com/consumer-trends/news/22972889/enrollment-in-snap-grocery-aid-is-dropping-faster-than-expected (2026-08-21).

findings.finding: Both listed natural-channel retailers reported negative traffic inside UNFI's Q4 window (2026-05-03 to 2026-08-01): Natural Grocers' quarter ended 2026-06-30 showed daily-average comps +1.2% built entirely on a +3.1% basket with transaction count -1.8% and gross margin down 60bp, and Sprouts' June quarter showed comps -1% with management citing weaker June trends — while UNFI's Natural segment (+4.4% in Q3) is the only growing part of the company and the pillar of the FY27 return-to-growth guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Nobody carries UNFI and NGVC in the same model — NGVC is a $335mm-a-quarter retailer and UNFI is a $31bn wholesaler, and the read-through runs the wrong way for a screener. If the market had made this link, the negative-unit-volume debate would be in the UNFI previews (which instead lead on the easy cyber comp and the +$0.62-vs-$(0.11) EPS optic) and UNFI's Natural-segment growth estimate would have been cut after 2026-08-06. NGVC itself fell 14% on the print, so the channel datapoint moved a price — just not this one.
findings.independence: Sprouts Farmers Market's June-quarter comp of -1% with explicit weaker-June commentary is a second, larger, independently sourced natural-channel datapoint: https://www.grocerydive.com/news/sprouts-farmers-market-second-quarter-results-self-distribution-new-store-openings-loyalty/826603/ . Cuts the other way, and I am counting it: Amazon's physical-stores line held +4% over the same window (see next finding).

findings.finding: Amazon's physical-stores net sales — the reported line for Whole Foods, UNFI's largest customer at roughly a quarter of net sales — were $5,794mm in the June-2026 quarter versus $5,595mm a year earlier, +4% and +4% excluding FX, essentially unchanged from the +4.6% March-quarter pace, covering two-thirds of UNFI's Q4.
findings.why_not_priced: Customer concentration is the standing bear case on UNFI and the reason the put skew sits at +6.97 points, but the one hard, contemporaneous, third-party measurement of that customer's volume during the quarter being reported sits in an Amazon 8-K exhibit that no UNFI preview cites. If it were priced, the previews would say Whole Foods sell-through was steady through July rather than treating the Whole Foods exposure as an unmeasured risk; instead the risk is discussed only through the 2032 contract term. It also removes one of the two live explanations for a Q4 revenue miss, leaving only the deliberate Allentown/Sturtevant optimisation.
findings.independence: The contract term itself is independently confirmed to May 2032, so this is volume news rather than renewal news: https://ir.unfi.com/news/press-release-details/2024/United-Natural-Foods-Inc.-Extends-Distribution-Partnership-with-Whole-Foods-Market-to-2032/default.aspx . Nothing else I found measures Whole Foods volume directly.

findings.finding: UNFI pulled its Q4/full-year report forward roughly three weeks against a stable four-year pattern — 2026-09-08 versus 2025-09-30, 2024-10-01 and late September in the two prior years — and announced the new date on 2026-08-10, the exact day the incoming CFO started, five and a half weeks after a 1 August fiscal year end.
findings.why_not_priced: Calendar aggregators carry the date, not the change in the date — the row reads 2026-09-08 with no memory that this company has reported Q4 in the last week of September or the first day of October every year since FY2022, so the timing shift leaves no trace in coverage or in the option chain. A company finalising a full-year audit and a fresh long-range plan five and a half weeks after year end, with a CFO four weeks into the job, is not behaving like one that needs time. I am scoring this small because I could not rule out the benign explanation: Barclays' Global Consumer Staples Conference runs 2026-09-09, the day after, and staples issuers routinely report just ahead of it — I could not confirm UNFI on that agenda either way.
findings.independence: Prior-year date confirmed in a separate, independently dated release: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20240911386565/en/United-Natural-Foods-to-Release-Fiscal-2024-Fourth-Quarter-Results-on-October-1-2024 (2024-09-11).

findings.finding: The initial FY27 guide — the single largest swing factor in this print — will be delivered by a CFO who started on 2026-08-10, four weeks before, as part of four senior changes in seven weeks around the fiscal year end: Matteo Tarditi moved off CFO to President/COO, Alfredo Luchini arrived as CFO from Carrier, supply-chain head Mark Bushway was announced as departing 2027-01-01, and Chief Corporate Affairs Officer Matthew Echols ceased in the role on 2026-08-24.
findings.why_not_priced: The personnel facts are in an 8-K, but the consequence for this specific print is not in any preview: UNFI's two 20%-class up-moves (2024-12-10 +20.02%, 2025-09-30 +18.45%) were both guide-setting prints delivered by Tarditi, who set FY26 deliberately low ($1.50-2.30 adjusted EPS) and raised the midpoint to $2.50 over three quarters. A first-print CFO inheriting a public $800mm FY28 target he did not set has an asymmetric incentive to anchor FY27 at the bottom of that path. If the market had focused on this, the 12.5% implied would be skewed toward a guidance-reset outcome rather than symmetric around a spot 21% off the high, and previews would be discussing who owns the FY27 number.
findings.independence: The Echols exit is a separate document (Form 4 with no transactions, 2026-08-27): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001020859/000162828026059263/wk-form4_1787862228.xml . This finding overlaps with the Q4-EBITDA-arithmetic finding above — both resolve into FY27 guide risk — and the two should be collapsed to roughly one and a half findings, not two.

searched_and_found_nothing: Whole Foods/Amazon insourcing or contract risk — the primary distribution agreement was extended in May 2024 to May 2032, so there is no near-term renewal event (https://ir.unfi.com/news/press-release-details/2024/United-Natural-Foods-Inc.-Extends-Distribution-Partnership-with-Whole-Foods-Market-to-2032/default.aspx)

A new DC closure or WARN notice inside the print window — the only live one is Sturtevant WI (443 jobs, WARN filed 2026-03-16, separations phased 20 June to early August 2026) and it was disclosed in March; the 716-job Schnecksville/Allentown PA closure and the Key Food contract exit are a JUNE 2025 story (https://www.wfmz.com/business/grocery-wholesaler-closing-lehigh-county-facility-700-layoffs-coming/article_529e4c56-e336-4d1a-9617-eb8a78cc5c28.html, published 2025-06-11) — I nearly filed it as a current-quarter finding before reading the date off the article itself

A service-level or fill-rate breakdown from the Joliet cloud-WMS cutover in summer 2026 — searched retailer, supplier and Reddit channels; every out-of-stock account traces back to the June 2025 cyber incident, nothing in May-August 2026

Balance-sheet or covenant stress — Q3 10-Q shows $1,202mm unused ABL capacity, net leverage 2.5x (lowest since FY2018), goodwill of only $19mm net of $727mm accumulated impairment so no impairment tail risk, and the 2026-06-18 Term Loan Amendment No. 5 repriced $371mm from SOFR+4.75% to SOFR+4.00%, i.e. the credit is getting better not worse (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1020859/000102085926000017/unfi-20260618.htm)

A retail-segment divestiture or Cub Foods sale process — the only 2026 transaction is three Cub stores to franchisee Jerry's Enterprises announced 2026-08-17 (https://www.grocerydive.com/news/unfi-selling-cub-foods-stores-jerrys-minneapolis-grocery-supermarkets/828011/), too small to matter and no held-for-sale reclassification in the Q3 10-Q

Short-squeeze fuel — short interest is 2.65mm shares / 4.48% of float at 2026-08-14 versus 3.8-3.95mm shares before the 2024-12-10 +20.02% print (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/UNFI/short-interest/), so the crowding that amplified the historical up-tails is materially smaller

Food-at-home inflation inflecting — BLS food-at-home CPI was +2.7% y/y in July 2026 and flat month-on-month, essentially the same pricing backdrop UNFI described in Q3, so no inflation surprise to the wholesale sales dollar
A large customer loss or win beyond the already-disclosed Key Food exit and the single-customer project that management said cycles by Q3 FY2027

Whether UNFI is on the Barclays Global Consumer Staples 2026-09-09 agenda, which would fully explain the report-date pull-forward — could not confirm either way from the conference schedule or UNFI IR
baseline_tension: Three of my five directional findings (cyber-clean EBITDA run-rate, SNAP, natural-channel traffic) point the same way as the +6.97-point put skew and the -6.65% run-in and are therefore the part most likely already in the price, which is exactly why I keep the headline number at a fifth of the 12.5% implied; the two that cut against the skew — Whole Foods volume holding +4% through the quarter and a report date pulled forward three weeks against a four-year pattern — are the genuinely unpriced half, and separately the short base at 4.48% of float is now a third smaller than before the two 20%-class up-prints in the baseline's own history, so I read the implied distribution as thinner in the right tail than that history implies.
